raf_home.text: There's a vehicle back to the airfield whenever you want. The track is rough and I apologise for all of it.
Head home to RAF Brize Norton?

then.text: Right-o. A long hop, a short brew and then Oxfordshire.

else.text: No rush. The runway isn't going anywhere, and neither is the lagoon.

then.text: The chapel's whitewashed and the graves are tended. The drum was playing again last night. I think it likes you.
A Ravanne. A little drum with a rattle behind it. Sega, on its own, in the dark. I never tire of hearing it.
Take this. A tiny ravanne for luck. Please remember that this island was a home first, and that its people want to come back, and say so.

else.text: You've heard the drum. Now catch the Ravanne that plays it, near the old copra floor at dusk or after dark, and bring it to me.

then.text: Whitewash and brushes. Marvellous. We'll do the chapel wall and the graves' markers, a little at a time.
Please stay until dusk. There's something here you should hear.
The light turns gold. From the old copra floor comes the slow beat of a drum, and a rattle behind it, and a triangle.
The stars are out over the lagoon. From the old copra floor comes the slow beat of a drum, and a rattle behind it, and a triangle.

else.text: It's too early for the music. Come back around dusk, when the light goes gold, and wait by the old copra floor.
The Chief at the Marina has the brushes and the whitewash. He'll want to see you fight first. It's an old Navy ritual, I think, and entirely made up.
{greeting} I look after the chapel and the cemetery for the community. It's an honour, and not an easy job.
East Point was a village. People were born here and baptised here, they worked here, danced here and were buried here. And then they were taken away.
If you want to help, speak to the Staff Officer at Naval Party 1002. Ask what's needed before the next visit.
